court: In the High Court of Madras
respondents: Inspector General of Registration of Tamilnadu and Others … Respondent(s).
advocates: For Respondent(s): Mr. U. Baranidharan, SGP (R1 to R 5)
judgment_text:
Writ petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking for issuance of a writ of mandamus to direct the respondents 1 and 2 herein to consider and pass orders on the appeal dated 18-12-2023 submitted by the Petitioner challenging the Order of the District Registrar (administration) in Na.Ka. No. 2179/Aa6/2022 dated 26-9-2022 and consequent Fraudulent encumbrances, namely, the Registration of release deed in Document No. 1530 of 2022 dated 9-11-2022 and Sale Deed in Document No. 1812 of 2023 dated 26-10-2023 on the file of SRO, Tharangambadi, Mayiladuthurai District relating to the Registered Settlement Deed dated 29-10-2010 in Document No. 1348 of 2010 on the file of SRO, Tharangambadi.

The Order of the Court was delivered by

Abdul Quddhose, J.:— This writ petition has been filed seeking for a limited relief. The petitioner seeks for early disposal of his appeal dated 18-12-2023 pending on the file of the respondents 1 and 2, within a time frame to be fixed by this Court.

2. Mr U. Baranidharan, learned Special Government Pleader, accepts notice on behalf of the respondents 1 to 5. Since no adverse orders are passed against the respondents 6 to 9, notice to them in this writ petition is dispensed with.

3. No prejudice will be caused to the respondents 1 and 2, if the petitioner's appeal dated 18-12-2023 is directed to be disposed of by them, within a time frame to be fixed by this Court, after hearing the objections of the respondents 6 to 9, and by adhering to principles of natural justice. Accordingly, this writ petition is disposed of by directing the respondents 1 to 2 to pass final orders, on merits and in accordance with law, on the petitioner's appeal dated 18-12-2023, after hearing the objections of the respondents 6 to 9, and by adhering to the principles of natural justice, within a period of 12 weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order. This Court is not expressing any opinion on the merits of the aforesaid appeal of the petitioner. No Costs.
